methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heirloom Carbon is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Lanzatech, ticker LNZA), including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology uses the $150M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding $285M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median valuation across these three peers is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulation of both methods supports a valuation range of $242M to $1.1B, with a median of $642M. The significant spread between the stage-progression result ($285M) and peer-median result ($1.0B) reflects two material uncertainties: the representativeness of the $150M raised figure as a current-stage valuation proxy, and the heterogeneity of technology risk and commercialization maturity within the climate-tech peer set. Stage and capital efficiency relative to peers will be the primary reconciling factors in narrowing this range.
